xerj ask: query a repo without cloning it

xerj ask "<question>", or just xerj "<question>", answers a question about an open-source project from a pre-indexed pack of that project, on your machine, and cites the file and line. Nothing is cloned or indexed locally: a pack is a snapshot of an index the hub already built at a pinned commit. Every answer names the corpus, the pin and the licence. It needs v1.0.0-rc.97 or later (install).

The first question

$ xerj "how does zstd pick a window size"
xerj hub: no node answers at http://localhost:9200; starting a local node on port 9300 (data: ~/.xerj/hub/node, log: ~/.xerj/hub/node.log)
xerj hub: node ready on port 9300 (pid 76)
xerj hub: pulling 'zstd' (20.1 MB) — one-time download, later questions answer locally
xerj hub: pulled zstd 01b7154f 21038204 → 8 indices, 7874 definitions
zstd  pin 2026-10-02 (18 days old)  mixed: BSD-3 (lib) / GPL-2.0 (cli)  zstd/lib/zstd.h:2487
ZSTDLIB_STATIC_API size_t ZSTD_DCtx_setMaxWindowSize(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, size_t maxWindowSize);
  approach-only licence (hint only: BSD-3 OR GPL-2 dual (verify at pin)): read, do not copy
zstd  pin 2026-10-02 (18 days old)  mixed: BSD-3 (lib) / GPL-2.0 (cli)  zstd/lib/compress/zstd_compress.c:2129
static size_t ZSTD_resetCCtx_internal(ZSTD_CCtx* zc, …
…

Captured on 2026-10-19 with rc.97 on Linux x86_64, in a fresh $HOME with nothing on :9200; … marks cut output. Three things happened:

  1. Routing. The client picked zstd itself, from the per-corpus term sketches in the signed catalogue and the lockfiles of the project you run it in. No hub server sees the question for routing.
  2. A node. Answers come from a local XERJ node. If nothing answers on XERJ_URL or localhost:9200, xerj ask starts one on a free port from 9300 up. If you already run a node on :9200, the pack is restored into that one.
  3. A pull, once. The pack came from GitHub Releases. Its ed25519 signature and SHA-256 were checked before anything was extracted; a tampered pack or catalogue is refused (exit 3). Later questions to the same corpus answer from the local pack.

Look up one definition

$ xerj ask --def ZSTD_compressBound
zstd  pin 2026-10-02 (18 days old)  mixed: BSD-3 (lib) / GPL-2.0 (cli)  zstd/build/single_file_libs/examples/roundtrip.c:36
size_t ZSTD_compressBound(size_t maxSrc)
  approach-only licence (mixed: BSD-3 (lib) / GPL-2.0 (cli)): read, do not copy
zstd  pin 2026-10-02 (18 days old)  mixed: BSD-3 (lib) / GPL-2.0 (cli)  zstd/lib/compress/zstd_compress.c:79
size_t ZSTD_compressBound(size_t srcSize)
  approach-only licence (mixed: BSD-3 (lib) / GPL-2.0 (cli)): read, do not copy
answered from: local pack
real 0m0.030s

A symbol question (--def, a bare identifier, or "what is the value of X") returns the declaration with its file and line. Other questions return ranked passages.

JSON for agents

$ xerj ask --def LZ4_compress_default --json
{"corpus":"lz4","pin_sha":"0774d05537f9762f838f7ab541b7765f1a729cb5","pin_date":"2026-10-02","age_days":18,
 "licence_spdx":"mixed: BSD-2 (lib) / GPL-2.0+ (rest)","licence_class":"approach-only","answered_from":"local_pack",
 "mode":"def","hits":[{"file":"lz4/lib/lz4.c","line":1481,"kind":"function",
 "text":"int LZ4_compress_default(const char* src, char* dst, int srcSize, int dstCapacity)", …}, …],
 "truncated":false,"warnings":["approach-only licence (mixed: BSD-2 (lib) / GPL-2.0+ (rest)): read, do not copy"]}

Over MCP the same flow is three tools on xerj mcp: xerj_hub_find, xerj_hub_def and xerj_hub_ask. xerj init also writes a xerj-hub skill for Claude Code that says when to ask the hub.

Options

OptionWhat it does
--corpus <slug>Skip routing and ask this corpus.
--def <SYMBOL>Exact definition lookup: file:line, declaration, value.
--howTreat it as a how-does-it-work question (ranked passages).
--filesList the relevant files with their licences.
--offlineNever touch the network: cached catalogue and packs only.
--no-fetchDo not download a pack for next time.
--hosted on|off|autoWhether the question may be sent to the hosted hub. Default auto: off inside a git repository, on elsewhere. Set --hosted off, or xerj hub config hosted off once, to keep every question on this machine. What the hosted hub API logs is listed under Privacy on hub.xerj.org/about.
--max-tokens NCap the answer at about N tokens.
--jsonPrint the answer as JSON.
--url <node>The node that holds the packs. Default XERJ_URL, then localhost:9200, else a local node is started.

Exit codes

CodeMeaning
0Answered.
1No match, or nothing to answer from. Say so rather than answering from memory.
2Usage error or unknown corpus.
3A pack failed verification (signature, SHA-256 or format). Nothing was restored.
4More than one corpus matches. The candidates are printed; re-run with --corpus <slug>.
5This build has no hub public key, so no pack can be verified. Nothing was downloaded.

Managing packs and the node

xerj hub status            # cached packs, the automatic node, the hosted setting, catalogue age
xerj hub pull <slug>       # download, verify and restore one pack
xerj hub sync              # refresh the catalogue, bring cached packs up to their pins
xerj hub sync --install-timer   # do that every 6 hours
xerj hub stop              # stop the node xerj ask started, and only that process
  • xerj ask downloads on its own only packs of 50 MB or less, and never a pack whose licence class is Excluded. For a bigger pack it prints the xerj hub pull line with the size.
  • The packs directory has a 4 GB budget; the least recently used packs are evicted first.
  • Pins age. Each hit prints the pin date and its age in days; xerj hub sync moves cached packs to the catalogue's current pins.

Licences on every hit

A corpus is either adapt-with-attribution (permissive and public-domain sources: adapt the code and credit it) or approach-only (GPL-family sources: read for the design, do not copy). Approach-only answers carry the "read, do not copy" warning on every hit, as in the zstd and lz4 output above. Closed standards are not admitted to the hub.

What you can ask today

The signed catalogue that xerj ask routes over held 14 corpora on 2026-10-18: act, age, agentops, aiohttp, alertmanager, arkworks-algebra, arroyo, astro, attack-mappings-explorer, autorag, avro, lz4, snappy and zstd. hub.xerj.org lists 513 live corpora; the others are used through a manifest with xerj corpus add and xerj code, described in Corpus Hub. For your own files, use xerj autoindex instead.

When not to ask

Skip retrieval for a fact the model can already state exactly. On popular, well-memorised libraries retrieval is neutral to harmful and only adds cost; it pays on niche, private and post-cutoff code (reference-coding case study).
